c.tagline: A remote oasis at the edge of Tassili n'Ajjer, home to some of the world's oldest and largest collections of prehistoric rock art

taxi.fareNote: Tassili n'Ajjer excursions require a licensed guide and permit, arranged in advance through a tour agency

emergency.note: Dial 17 for police and 14 for medical/fire emergencies; French is more useful than English with dispatchers

walk: The oasis town itself is small and walkable; Tassili n'Ajjer and the Tadrart require a multi-day guided trek or 4x4 expedition

safety.safety: Requires a licensed guide and permits for Tassili n'Ajjer excursions; check current travel advisories for far southeastern Algeria before visiting
safety.crime: Low crime in town; the main risks are desert travel logistics and remoteness
safety.note: Djanet is popular with adventure travelers, but trip planning here is more involved than in most of Algeria

solo.f: escorted tours only; town itself safe

hood_landmark.Djanet Old Town: Djanet's palm-shaded old town and market
hood_landmark.Tassili n'Ajjer Park Entrance: The gateway trailhead into Tassili n'Ajjer National Park
hood_landmark.Tadrart Rouge: The red sandstone arches and formations of the Tadrart
hood_landmark.Sefar Rock Art Site: The Sefar plateau's dense concentration of prehistoric paintings
hood_landmark.Erg Admer (dunes): The Erg Admer dune sea south of town

avoid.reason: Independent travel outside town is restricted — the desert toward the Libyan and Niger borders is off-limits, and Tassili n'Ajjer excursions require licensed local guides.

hood_desc: The small palm-oasis town center with most hotels, the market, and Tuareg craft shops; the base for organizing any expedition.
The trailhead into one of the world's largest concentrations of prehistoric rock art, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
A dramatic red sandstone wilderness of natural arches and dunes southeast of Djanet, reached by multi-day 4x4 expedition.
A remote plateau within Tassili n'Ajjer holding thousands of Neolithic paintings and engravings, reached only on foot with a guide.
A sand sea south of town popular for camel trekking and overnight desert camping.
lodging: Tour-agency lodges at the park entrance

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; desert supplies can be brackish or untreated.

transit.sys: No formal transit; travel is by licensed 4x4 guide vehicles
transit.hours: Daylight hours; desert travel is carefully planned around heat and light
transit.pay: Arranged in advance with a tour agency, typically pre-paid
transit.map: Not applicable; all excursions are guide-led
transit.note: Visiting Tassili n'Ajjer legally requires a registered guide and park permit

transport.air: Djanet Inedbirene Airport (VVZ), about 30 km from town, with domestic flights from Algiers
transport.bus: Very limited long-distance bus service; most visitors fly in
transport.car: Remote desert roads; independent driving without a guide is not recommended

net.m: Limited 3G in town, no coverage in Tassili n'Ajjer
net.w: Wifi available in a few hotels but often slow or absent
net.gb: ~$5-10 for a prepaid tourist SIM (passport required to register)
net.fwn: Wifi limited to a handful of hotels
net.ap: A Mobilis or Djezzy prepaid SIM, registered with your passport

tip.s: 10-15% is customary and expected for trekking guides
tip.r: Rounding up or 5-10% is appreciated, not obligatory
